servicios.resumen: Foot and walking check-ups as children grow, from their first steps to their teenage years.
que_es: A child's foot changes a great deal while it grows. Many things that worry parents, such as flexible flat feet in the early years, are a normal part of development and correct themselves.
A podiatry check-up helps to tell what is normal for the child's age from what should be monitored or treated, and gives advice on suitable footwear at each stage.
cuando_consultar: Your child complains of pain in the feet, ankles or legs, or tires more quickly than other children.
They trip or fall often.
They usually walk on tiptoe after the first few years.
Their feet point noticeably inwards or outwards.
Their shoes wear down very unevenly.
They have an ingrowing toenail or a verruca on the sole of the foot.
que_hacemos: Examination of the foot and leg, with the child lying down and standing.
Observation of how they walk.
An explanation for the family of what is normal for their age.
If needed: follow-up, exercises, footwear advice or custom insoles.

faq.p: My child has flat feet. Do they need insoles?
faq.r: Not always. In the early years the arch of the foot is still developing, and a flexible flat foot that doesn't hurt is usually normal. After the examination we'll explain whether it should be treated or simply monitored.

faq.p: At what age should the first check-up be?
faq.r: There is no set age. A good time is once your child walks confidently, or as soon as you notice something that worries you.

faq.p: What footwear is best for a child?
faq.r: In general, shoes that are flexible, light, the right size and that hold the foot securely. At the appointment we'll advise you according to your child's age and activities.

servicios.resumen: Regular check-ups and safe foot care for people with diabetes, to prevent wounds and spot problems early.
que_es: Over time, diabetes can reduce feeling and circulation in the feet. A small blister or a cut while trimming your nails can go unnoticed and become complicated.

A podiatry check-up shows the level of risk for each foot and allows it to be cared for safely. It complements the follow-up by your doctor and your health centre's nursing team; it does not replace it.
cuando_consultar: You have diabetes and have never had your feet checked.
You notice tingling, numbness or less feeling in your feet.
You have hard skin, corns or thickened nails that you can't safely look after yourself.
You have had a wound on your foot that was slow to heal.

aviso_urgente.titulo: When not to wait for your appointment
aviso_urgente.texto: See your doctor or go to A&E the same day if you have a wound that isn't getting better, an area that is red, hot or swollen, a change of colour in a toe (dark or bluish), a bad smell or a fever.

que_hacemos: Examination of sensation, pulses, skin, nails and the shape of the foot.
Assessment of your risk level and how often you should be checked.
Safe treatment of hard skin, corns and nails.
Advice on daily care and footwear.
If needed: insoles that spread the pressure under your foot.

faq.p: How often should I have my feet checked?
faq.r: It depends on your risk. It can range from once a year if your risk is low to every few months if it is high. We'll tell you after the first examination.

faq.p: Can I cut my nails and remove hard skin at home?
faq.r: Nails, yes, carefully and straight across, if you can see and reach them well. For hard skin, it's best not to use blades or corn plasters: with diabetes it's easy to injure yourself without noticing.

faq.p: What should I look for every day?
faq.r: Check your feet in good light (with a mirror if you can't reach): wounds, blisters, redness or changes in colour. Also check inside your shoes before putting them on.

servicios.resumen: An analysis of how you stand and walk, to understand what is causing discomfort in your feet, ankles or legs.
que_es: Many foot problems, and some ankle, knee or hip problems, are related to the way you stand or walk.
A biomechanical analysis looks at the structure of the foot and how it moves, to find the cause and decide on treatment. Not every case needs insoles.
cuando_consultar: Your heel hurts, especially in the first steps of the morning.
You have pain in the ball of the foot.
Your feet or legs get very tired when walking or standing.
You have ankle or knee discomfort that gets worse when walking or running.
You are about to start running or playing sport regularly.
que_hacemos: A conversation about your symptoms, your activity and your footwear.
Examination of the foot and leg on the couch.
Assessment of how you stand, at rest.
Analysis of how you walk and, if you play sport, how you run.
A clear explanation of the results and a treatment proposal.

faq.p: How long does the analysis take?
faq.r: Usually between 45 and 60 minutes, depending on the case. Bring the shoes you wear most and comfortable clothes.

faq.p: Does it always end with insoles?
faq.r: No. Depending on the results, treatment may be a change of footwear, exercises, insoles or a combination.

servicios.resumen: Insoles made for your feet based on a biomechanical analysis, for everyday use or for sport.
que_es: A custom insole (foot orthosis) is designed for your foot and for what you need: to spread pressure, improve how you stand or take the load off a painful area.
Unlike an off-the-shelf insole, it is made from a mould of your foot and the examination carried out beforehand.
cuando_consultar: After a biomechanical analysis shows that they may help you.
If you already wear insoles and they are worn out or no longer help.
que_hacemos: A biomechanical analysis first.
A mould of your foot.
Design and manufacture of the insole.
Fitting in your shoes.
A follow-up to check that they fit well.

faq.r: It depends on the material, how much you use them and your activity. At follow-ups we check their condition and let you know when they should be replaced.

faq.p: Can I use them in any shoe?
faq.r: They are designed for a specific type of footwear (everyday, sports or dress shoes). If you wear several types, we'll discuss it when making them.

servicios.titulo_seo: Chiropody in Barbate: corns, hard skin and nails
servicios.resumen: Treatment of hard skin, corns and nail problems, such as ingrowing or thickened toenails.
que_es: Chiropody treats the most common skin and nail problems of the foot: hard skin, corns, ingrowing toenails and thickened nails.
It is carried out with sterile instruments and adapted to each person, with particular care for older people and those with diabetes or circulation problems.
cuando_consultar: A corn or hard skin hurts when you walk.
You have an ingrowing toenail that is red or inflamed.
Your nails are thickened or misshapen and you can't cut them yourself.
You prefer your feet to be cared for by a healthcare professional.
que_hacemos: Examination and assessment of the cause (footwear, foot shape, the way you stand).
Removal of hard skin and corns.
Nail cutting and filing.
Treatment of ingrowing toenails.
Advice to stop them coming back.

faq.r: It is usually well tolerated. If an area is very sensitive or inflamed, we assess it and adapt the treatment.

faq.p: Why do corns keep coming back?
faq.r: Because they are usually caused by repeated rubbing or pressure. So as well as treating them, we look for the cause: footwear, foot shape or the way you stand.

servicios.resumen: Prevention and assessment of foot problems in people who run, walk or play sport regularly.
que_es: Sport greatly increases the loads the foot has to bear. Blisters, damaged nails, heel pain or discomfort that appears when training increases are common reasons to see a podiatrist.
A podiatry assessment aims to help you keep up your activity with less discomfort and a lower risk of injury.
cuando_consultar: You have foot or ankle pain that appears when you exercise.
You often get blisters, hard skin or black toenails.
You'd like advice on choosing sports shoes.
You are preparing for a race or increasing your training.
que_hacemos: Examination of the foot and of how you run or move in your sport.
Advice on sports footwear.
Sports insoles, if needed.
Treatment of hard skin, blisters and damaged nails.

faq.p: Do I need insoles to run?
faq.r: Not necessarily. Many people run without them. They are considered when there is discomfort or a change in how you stand that justifies them.
